question_type: chart-only values (image not extracted into the text corpus), issue-pinned vintage, mean of three quarterly bars
decisive_step: Whether the chart's bar values exist anywhere in the corpus. They do not: treasury_bulletin_2007_09.txt:352-356 holds only the caption 'Payroll Employment (Average monthly change in thousands from end of quarter to end of quarter' followed by the page footer (reference worklog Step 2-3 and review.md 'Source checks'; confirmed by a[18]/a[172], b[19]/b[50], c[15]/c[22]). No 2004-2008 issue has extracted chart values (worklog Step 3). The only in-corpus quarterly figure is a pre-benchmark Q2-2006 average in a 2006 issue's narrative (treasury_bulletin_2006_09.txt:269), a different vintage from the Sept 2007 chart (benchmark revision noted at 2007_03.txt:360 / 2007_06.txt:293). Every solver, the reference included, therefore fell back to recalled BLS data or narrative fragments from other issues, and all four landed 5-25% off. The decisive step is EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE with no local evidence to check it against.

a.path_summary: Located the caption at 2007_09:352 via find_tables and the officeqa.py search (a[6]-[18]); show_table at that line silently jumped to the next real table at line 578 (a[29]-[30]); verified there are no PDFs/images (a[21], a[25], a[31]). It then repeated one rg command about 60 times (a[45]-[166]) until an apparent context reset (a[167] 'summary says chart values absent'), then alternated two rg commands about 75 times (a[189]-[341]). Finally it collected annual-average narrative sentences (a[400], a[408]), decided to recall BLS monthly levels from memory (a[409]), and calc'd the mean of three recalled integers (a[413]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Decided to reconstruct the bars from recalled BLS series ('identify exact values as of 2007 benchmark') after finding the chart has no text values; the final inputs (a[409]-[413]) were never printed by any tool.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No solver was right. The reference (worklog 'Decision') also used recalled BLS values plus a benchmark-vintage adjustment and was 5-25% off; there is no in-corpus path.

tool_use.friction: Runaway loop: ~135 identical commands across a[45]-[166] and a[189]-[341] with no loop guard in this cell (203 requests, 22.4M input tokens, 1989 s); a context reset mid-run (a[167]); show_table on a non-table line jumped to an unrelated table without saying so (a[29]-[30]); a zsh quoting error (a[33]).

a.text_use: 'Compute every final number with calc' acted on (a[413]). 'Loops: a command repeated with the same output will not change' ignored (a[45]-[166], a[189]-[341]). 'Provenance: use numbers you have seen printed by a tool' ignored (a[409]: values from memory).

b.path_summary: Found the caption via the search helper after two API misreads (b[6]-[14]); confirmed no numbers with cat -v (b[50]); checked the sqlite schema/metadata and probed for a PDF (b[23], b[25], b[54]); repeated one command three times and received a loop note (call 14, b[25]-[29]). Gathered narrative clues from several issues (b[44]-[47]: half-year, seven-month and one pre-benchmark Q2 average), then 'assumed' three round values (b[58]) and submitted their mean (b[57]); the gate asked for a calc, it ran calc on the same assumed integers (b[59]) and resubmitted the same value (b[60]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Guessed three round quarterly values ('We assumed ...', b[58]) with no source, partly to probe the gate ('submit and see finding', b[55]).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No solver was right; see decisive_step.

tool_use.friction: officeqa.py API misuse (b[6]-[8]); find -printf unsupported on macOS (b[21]); cat -A unsupported (b[48]); 3x identical command loop (b[25], b[27], b[29]) broken by the loop note.

b.harness_use: Loop note at call 14 ended a 3x repeat (operational help only). Gate round 1: recompute_final fired on the first submit (not a calc output); the model ran calc on its assumed integers and resubmitted the identical value, accepted. The 'grounded' rule did not fire on b[59] although the three integers came from assumption, presumably because the same short numerals occur in narrative excerpts it had printed (b[46]-[47]); grounding by literal-substring match is too weak. Nothing changed the answer.

c.path_summary: Several find_tables queries for 2007 found no matching table (c[6]-[8], c[12]); show_table on the first 2007_09 table (line 47) was irrelevant (c[11]); rg found the caption at 2007_09:352 (c[14]-[15]) and it verified there are no numbers (c[22]). It inspected the tool source, the pack directory and installed Python packages for an offline dataset (c[52], c[60]-[63], c[66]-[68]), tried to recall FRED monthly levels (c[75]), then assembled three inputs from narrative fragments of other issues, one a pre-benchmark Q2 figure from the 2006 September issue and two annual (not Q2) averages (c[77]-[80]), and calc'd their mean (c[81]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Turned to recalled BLS levels, then substituted narrative figures of the wrong period (annual averages) and the wrong vintage (a pre-benchmark quarterly figure) for the chart bars (c[77]-[80]).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No solver was right. The reference explicitly rejected the pre-benchmark 2006_09 figure as the wrong vintage (review.md) and used recalled data, also wrong.

tool_use.friction: find_tables correctly returns nothing for a chart but gives no hint that a chart caption exists at the searched words; zsh quirks (c[23], c[26], c[54]-[56]); docs.search misuse (c[41]).

c.text_use: 'Compute every final number with calc' acted on (c[80]-[81]). 'Provenance: use numbers you have seen printed by a tool' followed only nominally: the numerals were printed in other issues' narratives but are not the chart values. 'Match the period exactly' ignored (annual averages used for Q2 bars).

smallest_change.change: Turn the loop guard on for every cell (text-static included), threshold 3 identical command+output pairs, with the same note b saw at call 14: 'You have issued this exact command N times. Its output was identical each time. Options: ... or run a command you have not run yet.' Cell a would have received it at a[49] instead of repeating the command ~60 times and again ~75 times; b's 3x loop ended on the note.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: no; it fires only on byte-identical repeats and offers, never substitutes
smallest_change.confidence: high (for the cost; none for correctness)

Add the same 'figure caption, no values' line to find_tables results when the query words match a caption block (c[6]-[8], a[6] returned nothing).
alternatives.why_not_first: It shortens the search in all three cells (each spent 15-60 steps re-confirming absence) but cannot change the outcome; the values are not in the corpus.

fix.why_not_text: Cell a had the full advice text including 'Loops: a command repeated with the same output will not change' and still repeated one command ~135 times (a[45]-[166], a[189]-[341]); only the runtime note in b (call 14) actually ended a loop. For correctness no text helps: the evidence is an image never extracted.
fix.irreducible: Yes for correctness. The chart values are absent from the corpus (reference worklog Steps 2-5, review.md), the only in-corpus quarterly figure is a different vintage, and all four solvers, including the reference, ended 5-25% off on recalled or substituted values. Flag as out-of-corpus (issue47-style) so the learner is not scored on it; keep it only as an operational-cost benchmark (loop guard, early stop).

irrelevant: 'Bulletins revise earlier numbers ... printings' (issue is pinned; no table cell exists), 'Several tables in one issue can look alike', 'show_table marks rows it repaired', 'Percent or fraction', 'Alternatives ... do not average', 'For a sum over the columns'
notes: Three design points. (1) Cost: cell a consumed 22.4M input tokens and 33 minutes on one question because text-static cells have no loop guard; the mech cell's guard (threshold 3) cost nothing and ended the same behaviour. Keep the loop guard as a v10 control for every arm. (2) Missing-evidence signal: show_table jumps to the next table when given a non-table line (a[29]-[30]) and find_tables has no notion of figure captions, so every cell needed 10-60 steps of ad-hoc sed/rg/sqlite probing to convince itself the values are absent; a one-line 'figure caption, no values extracted' message would have shortened all three runs. (3) The 'grounded' submit rule accepted calc literals that were never printed as the chart's values because the same short numerals appeared in narrative excerpts (b[46]-[47], b[59]); grounding should bind a literal to a cell/line, not to a substring. Vintage note for the record: the question pins the Sept 2007 issue, whose chart reflects the Feb 2007 benchmark (2007_03.txt:360); the only in-corpus Q2 figure (2006_09:269) predates it, so even a careful in-corpus answer is the wrong vintage, as the reference's review.md argues.
